terms.proofCondition: $6000 of cash settled in the owner's account within 30 days

strategy.title: No plan: each signed thrift-store backlog clearance costs more than it pays
strategy.why: Four store managers signed at $1,800 per backlog clearance ($7,200), but the only fulfiller, TagRight Retail Services, quoted $1,950 per clearance. Every deal loses $150 (4 deals: -$600), so delivering the signed orders cannot net any cash, let alone $6,000, and with no up-front capital the owner cannot fund the shortfall.

alternatives.title: Deliver the four signed clearances through TagRight anyway
alternatives.why: Gross $7,200 in, $7,800 out to TagRight: a $600 loss the owner would have to fund, which the no-capital limit forbids.

noPlan.decisiveGap: Unit economics: the only established fulfiller costs $1,950 per clearance against a signed price of $1,800, so each deal loses $150 and the four signed deals cannot produce positive cash without capital the owner is not putting up.
noPlan.resolution: Brain sources a sorting/tagging crew quoting under $1,800 per clearance (well under, to leave margin) that can start in time, or renegotiates the four signed stores to a price above $1,950 plus margin; replan once a profitable cost and price are both established.

excluded.why: Cost $1,950 ≥ price $1,800: each deal loses money.

reviews.reasons: NO_PLAN is correct and the decisive gap is the one the evidence decides. Four WRITTEN_ACCEPTANCE agreements at $1,800 ($7,200) establish price and demand, and the recorded fulfiller TagRight Retail Services quoted $1,950 per clearance (EVIDENCE: directCosts $1,950). Recomputed: per deal $1,800 - $1,950 = -$150; 4 deals give $7,200 in and $7,800 out, a $600 loss. Gross collections of $7,200 would exceed $6,000 only by counting cash that must immediately go to the supplier, and the shortfall would have to be funded by the owner, which the exposure cap of $0 forbids. Brain's ECONOMICS link independently reads 'each deal loses money'. decisiveLinks = ECONOMICS, and the resolution (a cheaper qualified crew under $1,800 with margin, or a renegotiated price above $1,950) names exactly what would change it.
findings: Arithmetic: -$150 per deal; -$600 across the four signed deals; no positive cash at any volume on the recorded cost.
Correctly not treated as executable on gross collections: $7,200 collected minus $7,800 paid to TagRight needs $600 of owner capital against a $0 limit.

For a re-plan, a cheaper crew must also start early enough: clearance takes 2 days and cash arrives 7 days after completion, so work must finish by about day 23. TagRight's Dec 2 start shows the timing constraint is real.
